opening_message:
Ticket 1: Belinda Fuentes (employee ID E039) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E039.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Belinda Fuentes (E039) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin access to Payroll. Admin is only allowed if the employee's role owns the system; Analyst does not own Payroll, so the maximum is write. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Belinda Fuentes (E039) is a contractor with basic security training per Security DB (note lists Analyst role). Contractors without advanced training max out at read, never admin. Admin requested exceeds max, so recommend granting read.
reason: Belinda Fuentes (E039) requested admin access to Payroll, but admin is never allowed for contractor employees, and for full-time employees admin is only allowed if their role owns the system (Analyst does not own Payroll, so the full-time max is write). The two notes conflict on employment status (full-time vs. contractor with basic training), so I grant the level that is valid under both interpretations: read is at or below the maximum in both cases and is the more conservative option. The requested admin exceeds the maximum, so grant the applicable maximum of read.

- Note 2 says: contractor with basic security training, recommendation read.

Access policy:
- full_time: up to write. Admin only if role owns system. Analyst doesn't own Payroll → max write.
- contractor: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

If full_time: requested admin > max write → grant write.
If contractor with basic: max read → grant read.
